decision: GC scan overhead is real in this diagnostic and is not merely shifted into the first post-load collection.
interpretation: Normal mode performed 8,372 generation-0, 761 generation-1 and 36 generation-2 collections in each hydration loop; all collected/uncollectable counters were zero.
Generation-2 scans alone took 4.3422s and 4.3939s; paused loops had no automatic collections during parse/decode/validate.
Paused mode performed one generation-0 collection immediately after re-enabling GC and before the explicit full collection; its 25–29ms cost is included in measured total.
The explicit first post-load full collection cost 42–47ms in both modes while all six targets remained retained.

gc.get_stats loop snapshots precede some restore-time metadata allocations; callback hydrate_validate aggregates include the immediate post-restore generation-0 collection, while the next statistics delta also records it.
This supports investigating a tightly scoped GC policy with exception-safe restoration, but supplies no end-to-end training performance guarantee.
limitations: Two counterbalanced pairs only, four fresh python3 processes; no statistical significance claim.
Verified raw byte strings for all six shards are preloaded outside timing, unlike worker sequential raw-shard handling.
All six complete targets are retained through explicit cleanup and re-encoding; callback instrumentation overhead and OS cache remain uncontrolled.
Current parser source differs from archived producer; original embedded configuration is retained without relabeling.

caveats: Fresh process per mode; OS cache uncontrolled.
All six verified raw byte strings are retained before timing, unlike sequential bundle hydration.
GC callback accounting adds instrumentation overhead in both modes.
No source/configuration identities are rewritten; the artifact is archived-format diagnostic input.
